from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and outline
        title = "The Core Intuition: Probability as Space"
        lines = [
            "Imagine all possibilities fit inside a unit square.",
            "The total area of this square equals one.",
            "We represent probability as a specific area within it."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        COLOR_SQUARE_OUTLINE = WHITE
        COLOR_SQUARE_FILL = "#333333"
        COLOR_PROBABILITY_AREA = "#3498DB" # Blue

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine all possibilities fit inside a unit square.
        # Draw a square outline (color: #FFFFFF) and fill it with dark grey (#333333).
        
        # Create square
        unit_square = Square(side_length=3.0, stroke_color=COLOR_SQUARE_OUTLINE, fill_color=COLOR_SQUARE_FILL, fill_opacity=1.0)
        # Using B2 to E5 as the container area to avoid Row A (titles) and Col 6 (clipping)
        self.place_in_area(unit_square, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Create(unit_square),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The total area of this square equals one.
        # Fade in the text 'Area = 1' at the center of the square.
        
        area_label = Text("Area = 1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        # Position label at center of square (grid center of B2-E5)
        # center is already set by place_in_area for unit_square
        area_label.move_to(unit_square.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(area_label),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We represent probability as a specific area within it.
        # Transform a portion of the square to blue (#3498DB), covering 10% of the total area.
        # Draw a line and label 'Event: 10% Probability' pointing to the blue area.
        
        # Calculate 10% of the square's area. 
        # If square is 3x3, area is 9. 10% is 0.9.
        # Width 3, Height 0.3 results in 0.9 area (10% of height).
        blue_rect = Rectangle(
            width=unit_square.width, 
            height=unit_square.height * 0.1, 
            fill_color=COLOR_PROBABILITY_AREA, 
            fill_opacity=1.0, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        # Position it at the bottom inside of the unit square
        blue_rect.move_to(unit_square.get_critical_point(DOWN), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Create label for the blue area
        # Label in Col 2 or 3, Target in Col 4? 
        # Following L003 Rule 3: Labels within 1 unit.
        # Target (blue rect) is roughly at D3/D4 level.
        event_label = Text("Event: 10% Probability", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PROBABILITY_AREA)
        # Place label below the square (Row F is avoided by L003, so let's put it on the side or just above F)
        # We'll place it slightly below the square area.
        self.place_at_grid(event_label, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Shift label so it doesn't overlap with the square
        event_label.shift(DOWN * 0.8)
        
        # Pointer line
        pointer = Line(
            start=event_label.get_critical_point(UP),
            end=blue_rect.get_center(),
            color=COLOR_PROBABILITY_AREA,
            stroke_width=2
        ).add_tip(tip_length=0.15)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PROBABILITY_AREA),
            FadeIn(blue_rect),
            Write(event_label),
            Create(pointer),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The Scenario: Prior Probabilities"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet a robot detective hunting for a Glitch-Bot.",
            "Only twenty percent of bots in this factory glitch.",
            "We split our square to show this prior belief."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Bounding box for the factory (using rows C to E and columns 2 to 5)
        # Dimensions: 3.0 wide, 2.0 high.
        factory_outline = Rectangle(width=3.0, height=2.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(factory_outline, 'C2', 'E5')
        
        # Descriptive label for the whole factory
        factory_label = Text("Robot Factory (Total Bots)", font_size=22, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(factory_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(factory_outline), Write(factory_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2 in red to match the "Glitch-Bot" color
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C")
        )
        
        # Divide the 3.0 unit width into 20% (0.6) and 80% (2.4)
        # Colors: red (#E74C3C) and green (#2ECC71)
        red_rect = Rectangle(
            width=0.6, height=2.0, 
            fill_color="#E74C3C", fill_opacity=0.8, 
            stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        green_rect = Rectangle(
            width=2.4, height=2.0, 
            fill_color="#2ECC71", fill_opacity=0.8, 
            stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        
        # VGroup for simultaneous placement using the 6x6 grid system
        split_square = VGroup(red_rect, green_rect).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(split_square, 'C2', 'E5')
        
        # Transition from outline to filled regions
        self.play(
            FadeIn(split_square),
            factory_outline.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3),
            FadeOut(factory_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to the third line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Add labels for each region: 'Glitch-Bot' and 'Normal-Bot'
        glitch_label = Text("Glitch-Bot (20%)", font_size=18, color="#E74C3C")
        normal_label = Text("Normal-Bot (80%)", font_size=18, color="#2ECC71")
        
        # Position labels in Row B above their respective rectangles (Col 2 and Col 4)
        self.place_at_grid(glitch_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(glitch_label), Write(normal_label))
        
        # Pulse the 'Glitch-Bot' label to emphasize the initial belief (Prior)
        self.play(Indicate(glitch_label, color="#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        TITLE_TEXT = "The Evidence: Conditional Likelihood"
        LECTURE_LINES = [
            "The detective uses a Spark Test on a bot.",
            "Ninety percent of Glitch-Bots spark when tested.",
            "But ten percent of Normal-Bots also spark.",
            "We slice the rectangles to show these likelihoods.",
            "Shaded areas represent the chance of seeing a spark."
        ]
        
        # Color definitions
        RED_BASE = "#E74C3C"      # Prior Red from Section 2
        GREEN_BASE = "#2ECC71"    # Prior Green from Section 2
        RED_SPARK = "#FF5555"     # Brighter Red for Likelihood
        GREEN_SPARK = "#55FF55"   # Brighter Green for Likelihood
        DIMMED = "#111111"        # Darkened for non-sparking regions
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = BLUE_B
        
        self.setup_layout(TITLE_TEXT, LECTURE_LINES)

        # Initialization of geometric components
        # We use a 1:3 ratio for Glitch (1 col) vs Normal (3 cols) to stay within grid 2-5
        # Total visual area: Rows B-E (4 units height)
        
        # Glitch-Bot Rectangle (Col 2)
        glitch_rect = Rectangle(width=1, height=4, fill_color=RED_BASE, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(glitch_rect, "B2", "E2")
        
        # Normal-Bot Rectangle (Cols 3-5)
        normal_rect = Rectangle(width=3, height=4, fill_color=GREEN_BASE, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(normal_rect, "B3", "E5")
        
        # Base labels
        glitch_label = Text("Glitch-Bots", font_size=20, color=RED_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(glitch_label, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        normal_label = Text("Normal-Bots", font_size=20, color=GREEN_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The detective uses a Spark Test on a bot."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(glitch_rect),
            FadeIn(normal_rect),
            Write(glitch_label),
            Write(normal_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Ninety percent of Glitch-Bots spark when tested."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED_SPARK)
        
        # Top 90% Spark area for Red: Height 4 * 0.9 = 3.6
        glitch_spark = Rectangle(
            width=1, height=3.6, 
            fill_color=RED_SPARK, fill_opacity=0.9, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        glitch_spark.move_to(glitch_rect.get_critical_point(UP), aligned_edge=UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glitch_spark, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "But ten percent of Normal-Bots also spark."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_SPARK)
        
        # Top 10% Spark area for Green: Height 4 * 0.1 = 0.4
        normal_spark = Rectangle(
            width=3, height=0.4,
            fill_color=GREEN_SPARK, fill_opacity=0.9,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        normal_spark.move_to(normal_rect.get_critical_point(UP), aligned_edge=UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(normal_spark, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "We slice the rectangles to show these likelihoods."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Creating visual slicing lines at the boundary
        slice_line_red = Line(
            glitch_spark.get_critical_point(LEFT + DOWN),
            glitch_spark.get_critical_point(RIGHT + DOWN),
            color=WHITE, stroke_width=4
        )
        slice_line_normal = Line(
            normal_spark.get_critical_point(LEFT + DOWN),
            normal_spark.get_critical_point(RIGHT + DOWN),
            color=WHITE, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(slice_line_red), Create(slice_line_normal))
        self.play(Indicate(slice_line_red, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR), Indicate(slice_line_normal, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Shaded areas represent the chance of seeing a spark."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Dim the lower regions (No-Spark zones)
        glitch_dim = Rectangle(
            width=1, height=0.4,
            fill_color=DIMMED, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(glitch_rect.get_critical_point(DOWN), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        normal_dim = Rectangle(
            width=3, height=3.6,
            fill_color=DIMMED, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(normal_rect.get_critical_point(DOWN), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Specialized Likelihood Labels (True Positive vs False Positive)
        tp_label = Text("True Positive", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        # Position centered in the top section of the Red rectangle
        self.place_in_area(tp_label, "B2", "C2", scale_factor=0.7)
        tp_label.shift(UP * 0.2) # Fine-tune to center vertically in the spark area
        
        fp_label = Text("False Positive", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        # Position centered in the top section of the Green rectangle
        self.place_at_grid(fp_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.7)
        fp_label.shift(UP * 0.2) # Fine-tune to center vertically in the spark area

        self.play(
            FadeIn(glitch_dim),
            FadeIn(normal_dim),
            FadeIn(tp_label),
            FadeIn(fp_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Geometric Update: Slicing the Universe"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Suddenly, the robot detective sees a bright spark.",
            "Non-sparking possibilities are now impossible in our world.",
            "We discard the bottom sections of our probability square.",
            "Our universe shrinks to only the shaded regions.",
            "Only two possible paths to a spark remain."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from previous sections
        RED_SPARK = "#FF5555"
        GREEN_SPARK = "#55FF55"
        NEAR_BLACK = "#111111"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Grid constants for the 1x1 probability square
        # Positioned in area B2 to E5 (width 3, height 3)
        square_width = 3.0
        square_height = 3.0
        tl_point = self.grid["B2"]
        
        # --- Create Geometric Components (Initial State) ---
        
        # 1. True Positive (Glitch-Bot + Spark): 20% width, 90% height
        tp_w = 0.2 * square_width
        tp_h = 0.9 * square_height
        tp_rect = Rectangle(width=tp_w, height=tp_h, fill_color=RED_SPARK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
        tp_rect.move_to(tl_point + np.array([tp_w/2, -tp_h/2, 0]))
        tp_label = Text("True Positive", font_size=12, color=WHITE).move_to(tp_rect.get_center())

        # 2. False Positive (Normal-Bot + Spark): 80% width, 10% height
        fp_w = 0.8 * square_width
        fp_h = 0.1 * square_height
        fp_rect = Rectangle(width=fp_w, height=fp_h, fill_color=GREEN_SPARK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
        fp_rect.move_to(tl_point + np.array([tp_w + fp_w/2, -fp_h/2, 0]))
        fp_label = Text("False Positive", font_size=12, color=WHITE).move_to(fp_rect.get_center())

        # 3. No Spark Red: 20% width, bottom 10% height
        ns_red_h = 0.1 * square_height
        ns_red_rect = Rectangle(width=tp_w, height=ns_red_h, fill_color=NEAR_BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
        ns_red_rect.move_to(tl_point + np.array([tp_w/2, -tp_h - ns_red_h/2, 0]))

        # 4. No Spark Green: 80% width, bottom 90% height
        ns_green_h = 0.9 * square_height
        ns_green_rect = Rectangle(width=fp_w, height=ns_green_h, fill_color=NEAR_BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
        ns_green_rect.move_to(tl_point + np.array([tp_w + fp_w/2, -fp_h - ns_green_h/2, 0]))

        # 5. Universe Frame
        universe_frame = Rectangle(width=square_width, height=square_height, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        universe_frame.move_to(tl_point + np.array([square_width/2, -square_height/2, 0]))

        # Groups for animation
        sparking_regions = VGroup(tp_rect, fp_rect, tp_label, fp_label)
        non_sparking_regions = VGroup(ns_red_rect, ns_green_rect)
        
        # Initial display (representing end of Section 3)
        self.add(sparking_regions, non_sparking_regions, universe_frame)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Suddenly, the robot detective sees a bright spark.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        spark_star = Star(n=8, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(spark_star, "B4") # Centered above the square
        
        self.play(FadeIn(spark_star), Indicate(spark_star, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Non-sparking possibilities are now impossible in our world.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(
            non_sparking_regions.animate.set_fill(BLACK, opacity=1).set_stroke(opacity=0),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We discard the bottom sections of our probability square.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(non_sparking_regions),
            FadeOut(universe_frame),
            spark_star.animate.fade(1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Our universe shrinks to only the shaded regions.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        # Shift the remaining blocks to the center of the right-side area

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "From Geometry to Formula", 
            [
                "This geometric process is exactly what Bayes' Theorem describes.",
                "The numerator represents the specific shaded Glitch-Spark area.",
                "Dividing by the total shaded area gives the posterior."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR = "#F1C40F"  # Gold as per Section 5 instructions
        FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR = "#3498DB" # Blue for contrast
        EQUATION_COLOR = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the equation P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E) in white (#FFFFFF).
        
        # We break the equation into parts for easier boxing later
        # Part 0: P(H|E) = 
        # Part 1: Numerator (P(E|H)P(H))
        # Part 2: Fraction line
        # Part 3: Denominator (P(E))
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(H|E)", "=", "{P(E|H) P(H)", "\\over", "P(E)}",
            color=EQUATION_COLOR
        )
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a box around the numerator and point it to the 'True Positive' area.
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR)
        
        # Representative 'True Positive' area (Glitch-Spark)
        # Using a rectangle to mimic the geometric concept
        true_positive_rect = Rectangle(
            width=1.0, height=0.6, 
            fill_color=GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, 
            stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        tp_label = Text("Glitch-Spark", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        tp_group = VGroup(true_positive_rect, tp_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(tp_group, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Target the numerator specifically in the MathTex
        # formula[2] is P(E|H)P(H)
        num_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula[2], color=GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        num_arrow = Arrow(
            start=num_box.get_critical_point(UP),
            end=tp_group.get_critical_point(DOWN),
            color=GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR,
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tp_group),
            Create(num_box),
            GrowArrow(num_arrow)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(formula[2], color=GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a box around the denominator and point it to the 'Total Evidence' area.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR)
        
        # Representative 'Total Evidence' area (Glitch-Spark + False Positives)
        # Showing it as a larger composite rectangle
        total_evidence_rect = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.6, fill_color=GLITCH_SPARK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5),
            Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.6, fill_color=FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        total_evidence_rect.set_stroke(WHITE, width=2)
        
        te_label = Text("Total Shaded Area", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        te_group = VGroup(total_evidence_rect, te_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(te_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Target the denominator specifically in the MathTex
        # formula[4] is P(E)
        den_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula[4], color=FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        den_arrow = Arrow(
            start=den_box.get_critical_point(DOWN),
            end=te_group.get_critical_point(UP),
            color=FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR,
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(te_group),
            Create(den_box),
            GrowArrow(den_arrow)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(formula[4], color=FALSE_POSITIVE_COLOR))
        self.wait(3)

        # Final state cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
outline.target_audience: University students or advanced high school students with a basic grasp of probability

sections.title: The Core Intuition: Probability as Space
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept: Probability is not just a number, but an 'area' within a total space of possibilities. We represent the entire world of possibilities as a 1x1 square (Area = 1).
sections.example: Imagine a 10x10 grid representing a forest. If 10% of the forest contains Rare Blue butterflies, we color 10% of the square's area blue. This is our 'Prior' belief before seeing any evidence.

sections.title: The Scenario: Prior Probabilities
sections.content: Establish a base rate (Prior) using a character-driven example. Split the square vertically into two rectangles based on the initial probability of two competing hypotheses.
sections.example: A robot detective is looking for a 'Glitch-Bot'. In a factory, 20% are Glitch-Bots (Small Rectangle) and 80% are Normal-Bots (Large Rectangle). Visually, the square is now split 2:8.

sections.title: The Evidence: Conditional Likelihood
sections.content: Introduce new evidence that has different 'hit rates' for each hypothesis. Graphically, we slice the horizontal axis of our existing rectangles. This creates sub-areas representing 'True Positives' and 'False Positives'.
sections.example: The detective uses a 'Spark Test'. 90% of Glitch-Bots spark, but 10% of Normal-Bots also spark by accident. We shade the top 90% of the Glitch-Bot rectangle and the top 10% of the Normal-Bot rectangle.

sections.title: The Geometric Update: Slicing the Universe
sections.content: When evidence occurs (the 'Spark' happens), the 'non-sparking' areas of our square vanish. They are no longer possible. Our 'universe' of possibilities shrinks to only the shaded areas.
sections.example: The robot sparks! We visually discard the bottom (non-sparking) parts of the square. We are left with a thin slice from the Normal-Bots and a tall slice from the Glitch-Bots.

sections.title: The Posterior: Re-normalizing the World
sections.content: The final step of Bayes' Theorem: Re-stretching the remaining area to fill a 1x1 square again. The 'Posterior' probability is the ratio of the 'True Evidence' area to the 'Total Evidence' area.
sections.example: We compare the area of (Glitch-Bots who spark) against the total area of (All bots who spark). Even though the test is 90% accurate, because Normal-Bots were so common, the resulting 'New Area' for Glitch-Bots might only be 69%.

sections.title: From Geometry to Formula
sections.content: Translate the visual stretching and slicing into the algebraic form of Bayes' Theorem, showing how each term corresponds to a geometric transformation.
sections.example: P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E). We show that the numerator is the 'True Positive' area and the denominator is the 'Total Shaded' area.
